keyProps.createChangeEventDetails(reason, event?,: Builds a cancellable change-event details object. `reason` keys the native event type (see reasons record); `customProperties` are merged into the returned object (Base UI uses this for extra fields such as Tabs' activationDirection).
keyProps.createGenericEventDetails(reason, event?: Same shape without the cancellation/propagation utilities ({ reason, event } + customProperties).
keyProps.BaseUIChangeEventDetails<Reason, CustomP: { reason, event, cancel(), allowPropagation(), isCanceled, isPropagationAllowed, trigger } & CustomProperties

controlled: This is the object a controlled component hands to its change callback: onXChange(value, eventDetails). Consumers read eventDetails.reason to distinguish user input from automatic fallbacks, eventDetails.cancel() to veto Base UI's own handling, eventDetails.allowPropagation(), and eventDetails.trigger for the originating element.
notableDifferences: React Aria hands change callbacks a bare key/value (e.g. onSelectionChange(key)) or a PressEvent; Base UI wraps every change in an event-details object carrying reason + cancellation. RAC's event.continuePropagation() corresponds to allowPropagation(); canceling a change maps to cancel() (RAC has no equivalent for automatic-fallback reasons).
Public-importable but undocumented (only reachable via the ./internals/* subpaths): type import is idiomatic via `import type { BaseUIChangeEventDetails } from '@base-ui/react/types'`.
Automatic changes cannot be canceled — cancel() is a no-op for reasons 'initial', 'disabled', 'missing'.
